icon.description: A Phosphor icon name (phosphoricons.com), the app's own icon set

interactive.description: Its boards' firmware runs in the app

chips.description: The parts it is about, as people name them

source.description: Where it began, when not here

open.description: github: the app reads its folder from GitHub at the published commit (sources not ours to ship, e.g. GPL); default: its files are published with it

status.description: ready: orderable and flashable as it is (every board here is: an interactive board that only runs in the app is not published)

flash.description: How the ordered board takes its firmware

expect.description: What its programs must show or do in the laboratory (PCBKit's lab.simulate `expect`): run for `seconds` of device time in five phases, the report's `expected.met` must be true. The lab's registry count: a board that works, not one that only runs.

console.description: Text a serial terminal must have received, each

frames.description: Displays by component, and the pictures each must have drawn at least

toggles.description: Ports a program must have driven both low and high, as processor.port (U1.PB5)

lit.description: Visuals lit at the end of some phase (an indicator, a digit, a pixel, a servo driven), by component

responds.description: Inputs its programs must answer, each: a button or switch by component (or key:Name), pressed from the run's middle phase and released at the next, must change what some later phase shows (displays, lights, servos, console text) against the same run without it

corners.description: What its programs must show or do instead at a temperature where they react to it (a thermostat's heater on in the cold): a corner's expectation replaces this one there. Every board is also run at -40 and 85 °C; one with no entry for a corner must meet this expectation there.
